name: Single Ventricle Physiology

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Criteria for Single Ventricle Physiology

criteria.description: Presence of only one functional ventricular chamber supporting systemic and pulmonary circulation
Echocardiographic evidence of absent or hypoplastic second ventricle
Cyanosis and signs of congestive heart failure in neonatal period
Hemodynamic assessment confirming single ventricle physiology and pulmonary blood flow

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of one functional ventricle confirmed by imaging plus clinical signs consistent with single ventricle physiology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography and cardiac MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: Due to mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

common.notes: Secondary to pulmonary overcirculation or congestion
Due to heart failure and fatigue
Resulting from chronic hypoxia and cardiac insufficiency

occasional.notes: May develop secondary to ventricular dysfunction

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating heart failure
imaging: Cardiac MRI confirming ventricular morphology and flow dynamics
Chest X-ray demonstrating cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; associated with various congenital syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing ventricular hypertrophy or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Severe hypoplasia of left-sided cardiac structures
Common atrioventricular valve with septal defects
Two ventricles present but with abnormal septation

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Progressive decline in exercise tolerance or feeding
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Mertens L, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Congenital Heart Disease in Adults. Wiley-Blackwell; 2013.
American Heart Association. Congenital Heart Defects Fact Sheet. 2022.
